question.problem:
Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-{x}^{2}}4x{e}^{8y-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$

current_example.problem: Change the order of integration and evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle{\int_0^{1} \int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1 } 9\sqrt{y^3+1}\,\textrm{d}y\,\textrm{d}x}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/1045aaad8025b20309b92477b4a1cf98e138064210c6fbc960c64ec26c9951df.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad \sqrt{x} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y = \sqrt{x} 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x=y^2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y^2 \big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/40cbaaff270daddf4b60115cc272fbc8b165b83b8823d19de2c19802617ebdb4.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}9\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{y}^{3}+1}[x\,]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}3{y}^{2}({y}^{3}+1)^{1/2}\,dy \\  & =3{[\frac{2}{3}({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[2({y}^{3}+1)^{3/2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =2(2)^{3/2}-2 \\  & =4\sqrt{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$
